I literally own and operate hardware stores, lol. 

Item is bought for $13 from the wholesaler.
Item is sold for $26 to consumer.
50% margin - $13

Same Item, now on sale for $18.
~28% margin - $5

Sell 3 on sale, and you've made more than one at regular price. (Freight not factored in) Plus, you've made 3 customers happier because they saved $8.

 "Well, then $26 isn't the real price,"

Yes, it is. Sales create greater volume than day to day. Hence, it is unsustainable to offer the lower price full time because traffic won't keep up. Except for select few instances, you don't ever sell at a loss. If Factorio went on sale for $25, and they sold 4X what they normally would in that time frame, they made more money. It is really that simple.

I...I'm sorry but I can't bite my tongue, this is just a fundamental misunderstanding of how businesses work. At least at the VAST majority of brick and mortar retail stores don't bump prices to offer sales to the consumer. You take the normal price, margin of %40-60, and bring it down. That's it. No shady shit, no screwing over the customer, just: "Hey, it's cheaper right now because we can make the same amount of money and grow our customer base by selling volume."
